channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: Building Clockwork: An AI-Native 2D Game Engine Verified End-to-End with Kane CLI
item.description: Clockwork packs scene building, behaviors, rules, HUD design and playtesting into one browser app, with Kane CLI driving real Chrome to prove the editor and its games work end to end.

item.title: Download Rank Isn't Revenue: What 90 Days of App Store Charts Say About Mobile Games
item.description: Recording App Store charts in 170+ countries every day, the author shows how a game can lose most of its new players and still keep its revenue — three cases that expose the real gap between download rank and actual income.

item.title: Resident Evil 4 remake dominates current-gen remake sales with 16.8M copies, Steam's long tail powers revenue
item.description: New estimates from market analysis firm Alinea put Resident Evil 4 remake at 16.8 million copies sold, with Steam's long tail doing much of the revenue work.

item.title: Hire an Unreal Engine Developer: Costs and Options
item.description: The article compares the costs of hiring Unreal Engine developers as freelancers, through agencies or studios, or as full-time employees, helping small teams budget the hire.

item.title: Isometric Warsaw turns open city data into a playful Three.js map
item.description: This Three.js project turns open city data into a playful pixel-art isometric map of Warsaw, explaining the choices behind its look, navigation and flight mode.

item.title: Unity & Unreal Change The Way You Access Assets
item.description: The latest Unity and Unreal releases both overhaul how developers access assets — Unity's new Asset Library plugin reworks the Asset Store flow — so check how your workflow is affected.

item.title: Closing the Loop: How Clockwork's Built-in AI Agent Uses Kane CLI to Verify the Games It Builds
item.description: Clockwork's built-in agent doesn't trust its own word that it "added coins" — it has Kane CLI play the result in a real browser and return a typed verdict, a model for end-to-end verification of AI-built games.

item.title: Recreating the Scale Model Look of a Rally Diorama in Houdini
item.description: Will Hoskin walks through recreating the look of a handmade rally diorama in 3D, using Houdini's procedural tools to craft cotton dust, wire trees, and plastic figures.

item.title: Turning Whimsical 2D Town Into Cozy 3D World
item.description: Pedro Henrique Placido Silva explains how he turned a charming fantasy town from a 2D illustration into a 3D scene, covering modeling, texturing, vegetation, and the final render.

item.title: Flutter Flame Tutorial: Build Your First 2D Game (Beginner Guide)
item.description: If you already know Flutter, you're closer to shipping your first game than you think — this beginner guide walks you through building a 2D game with the Flame engine.

item.title: Turning a Real Map into a Pixel World
item.description: When the map itself is the game board, grey roads and a blue dot are not enough — the author shares how Kurukuru turned OpenStreetMap data into a pixel-art campus world while keeping real roads, buildings, and GPS positions intact.

item.title: How to export WAV files and ZIP archives entirely in the browser with vanilla JavaScript
item.description: A walkthrough of building a small browser tool that generates retro game sound effects and exports several variations as WAV and ZIP files with vanilla JavaScript — no backend or account needed.

item.title: Crouch y capas de tronco superior con Motion Matching en Unreal Engine 5
item.description: A step-by-step guide to implementing crouch and upper-body animation layers with Motion Matching in Unreal Engine 5, with screenshots and explanations for every step.

item.title: Fixing sprite atlas metadata errors in Unity / Godot / Phaser — offline, without re-exporting
item.description: Misaligned sprites are usually a metadata problem, not a broken image — this walkthrough covers four real fault patterns and shows which JSON or XML field to fix offline, no re-export needed.

item.title: PC Engine CD BIOS Devlog: The Next Observed Blocker Is $2C, Not a Compatibility Milestone
item.description: A developer logs progress on an open-source System Card replacement for the PC Engine CD, walking through the latest technical blocker and what to check next.

item.title: I Built a Tween Library Faster Than LitMotion for Unity
item.description: MyMotion is the author's own Unity tween library with an API compatible with LitMotion for easy migration; its Burst-compiled data-oriented core beats LitMotion in all 17 benchmark tests.

item.title: Choosing a Game Engine Before You Hire: A Decision Sheet for Founders Building a Team in India
item.description: A decision sheet for founders hiring a team in India: pick target devices before picking an engine, and weigh hiring, cost and platform trade-offs up front.

item.title: How a Rust civ sim stays deterministic with WebAssembly SIMD and threads
item.description: A browser civilization sim written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly; the author breaks down the fixed tick order and spatial indexing that keep the world evolving identically with SIMD or threads enabled.

item.title: Ensō Engine 1.1: a free Blender build for anime and NPR
item.description: Mix 3D Design released Ensō Engine 1.1, a free open-source Blender build tailored for anime and non-photorealistic rendering.

item.title: Localizing a Game for Turkish: the Dotted I, Suffixes on Placeholders and Other Engine Problems
item.description: Turkish looks like an easy Latin-alphabet locale until misspelled menus, broken item messages, and crashes only Turkish players can reproduce show up — the article unpacks each engineering pitfall.
